subject: Request: carveout for customer-managed connectors (hybrid/VPC/on-prem) — Cascade Bio
messages:
From: Emily Rios <emily.rios@cascadebio.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Noah Singh <noah.singh@cascadebio.com>, cascade-bio-security@cascadebio.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Carveout request for customer-managed connectors / network boundary

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. We like Redwood’s hybrid model but have one blocker from our security and procurement teams. Cascade runs sensitive workloads inside a vetted on-prem cluster and routes inference through a customer-controlled connector (e.g., an on-prem proxy + VPC egress). Our security team requires that any SLA language explicitly exclude latency/outage consequences caused by our on-prem network or the customer-controlled connector.

Specifically they asked for two things:
- A statement that Redwood’s uptime and latency SLOs apply only to the Redwood-managed portion of the stack (model serving runtime and control plane inside Redwood’s VPC).
- Explicit shared-responsibility language that exempts Redwood from SLA credits when the incident is attributable to: our on-prem network, a customer-managed proxy, or third-party on-prem appliances.

I’ve attached a high-level network diagram to show how our connector sits in the path. Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept carveout language like this and, if so, provide proposed wording we can take to procurement? This is on the critical path for our PO.

Appreciate any examples or precedent you can share.

Best,
Emily

Attachments: network-diagram.pdf

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rios <emily.rios@cascadebio.com>
Cc: Noah Singh <noah.singh@cascadebio.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Carveout request for customer-managed connectors / network boundary

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the clear diagram and the write-up. Short answer: yes, Redwood can accept carveouts for customer-managed networking components, but we need to capture precise language so both sides (legal + security) know what is in scope vs out of scope.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll loop in our infra/product legal partner to draft suggested SLA carveout language based on your three bullet points.
2) If you can confirm which Redwood endpoints (region/cluster) the connector talks to and whether you’ll use our VPC peering or a public egress path, that will help tighten the scope.
3) I’ll send a short mutual-action doc that includes the proposed wording and a deploy checklist for the connector.

I’m attaching a template MA (mutual-action) we typically use for hybrid deployments — it includes sample shared-responsibility clauses and monitoring handoff points. If that looks okay I can route the final wording through legal and security by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this.

— Grace O’Connor

Quick asks:

Keep it tight: define the Redwood-managed components and enumerate customer-managed items (on-prem networks, proxies, transit providers, third-party appliances). Also indicate what evidence we would accept to attribute an outage to customer infrastructure.

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed this with infra and legal. Below is proposed contract language we are comfortable including in the MA/SLA for Cascade Bio’s hybrid deployment. This is intentionally narrow and evidence-based so it’s operationally actionable:

--- Proposed carveout language (editable) ---
"Redwood’s Service Level Objectives (SLOs) for availability and request latency apply solely to Redwood-managed components, defined as Redwood’s control plane, model serving runtime, and any Redwood-managed edge/ingress endpoints. The following components are explicitly out of scope for Redwood’s SLOs and any associated SLA credits or refunds: (1) Customer-managed on-premise networks, routers, switches, or firewalls; (2) Customer-operated proxy or connector software and any third-party appliances or transit providers under the direct control of the Customer; and (3) Any network egress, transit, or routing decisions made by the Customer or its network providers that affect reachability between the Customer’s environment and Redwood ingress endpoints.

Attribution and Evidence: Redwood will rely on a combination of telemetry and mutually agreed evidence to attribute incidents. Acceptable evidence includes: server-side logs showing successful receipt of requests at Redwood ingress, traceroute outputs demonstrating packet loss external to Redwood-managed prefixes, and vendor incident reports when a third-party transit provider is implicated. Where mutual evidence cannot be produced, parties will engage the dispute resolution procedure in section X of the agreement."

--- end proposed language ---

Operational notes:
- We will instrument and share edge reachability logs for a 24-hour window around incidents if requested; please confirm which RBAC role will receive those logs.
- For latency SLOs, we propose excluding degradation attributable to customer-side queuing or network traversal; we can add a sample metric threshold (e.g., >50ms tail added inside customer network) if you want a numeric trigger.

Next steps:
1) If this language looks acceptable, reply with any edits and confirm the email address for delivery of reachability telemetry.
2) I’ve attached a ready-to-sign MA that includes this language and a DocuSign link to start signatures.

If you prefer, we can also arrange a 30-minute sync with our infra engineering and your security team to walk through instrumentation and evidence collection.

Best,
— Grace O’Connor
